title: The Voices Beneath the Water · Episode 24: Who the Opening Is For

planning.voiceReason: Being seen and accepted matters more than outward appearance.
planning.desire: A newly introduced resident couple prepares an opening display of community photographs and memories. One partner hides from the camera, convinced that wrinkles and ageing make them unworthy of being seen. A younger adult worries about acne; Jon listens instead of offering easy reassurance. They choose photographs that show relationships and work, not idealized appearances.
planning.payoff: The display honours real people across generations, including optional private memories of past losses without changing who survived.
planning.convergence: Every target gets two distinct meaningful uses on the common path; optional choice text is not the sole exposure. Choices change tone, approach and acknowledgment, not permanent plot branches.
planning.obstacle: Others need room to choose, while Jon is tempted to organize their feelings for them.
planning.dramaticChange: Jon gives up control and listens to a concrete request.
sceneActivities: Jon puts down his camera to listen; residents select photographs after explicit consent.
planning.listenerTurn: Pair → Luma asks to choose → listener Jon → hand leaves camera → pair.

continuation.end: The residents Luma and Daro and young adult Nia choose community photographs after Jon listens to appearance worries and respects consent. They choose images of helping and relationships; nobody is required to appear or disclose private memories. The centre remains closed pending final inspection. Water and historical consequences are unchanged.
continuation.nextStart: Final inspection clears the centre for its agreed use. An enthusiastic young adult volunteer overwhelms the opening programme with their favourite music, while a neighbour worries that quieter visitors will be left out. Jon helps them make room for one another. The shared meal, garden route, learner writing and photographs become parts of one community event.
